condition_definition: v2: identical to Condition B v2 (same MMS/VITS Yoruba checkpoint, same recordings, split, training budget, seed, checkpoint-selection rules, evaluation criteria, and frozen duration predictor) with exactly one further experimental change: explicit orthographic H/M/L tone and syllable-boundary auxiliary supervision, derived from the verified word/syllable alignment data already reviewed by Mary Adelua, added on top of the ordinary VITS objectives. Tests whether this explicit supervision improves pronunciation beyond ordinary fine-tuning with the same audio -- not whether a language-naive model can learn Yoruba (that is a separate, future, explicitly out-of-scope experiment). v1 (unfrozen duration predictor) produced skipped syllables that a decoding-noise diagnostic (duration_diagnostic/) showed were not a decoding artifact; the duration predictor is now frozen at its known-reliable pretrained state, same as Condition B v2. The syllable-boundary auxiliary loss remains meaningful with the predictor frozen: gradients still flow back through it into the text encoder, training it to produce representations the frozen predictor interprets correctly, rather than trying to move the predictor itself.

implementation.implementation_policy: Record resolved commit IDs and source-tree SHA-256 before execution
implementation.required_entrypoint: original VITS train.py with only the frozen single-GPU, accumulation, development-evaluation, early-stopping, provenance, and tone/syllable-auxiliary patches
implementation.auxiliary_supervision_note: Tone: a linear classifier head reads the text encoder's per-token hidden state (enc_p output, before duration expansion), average-pooled per syllable, trained with cross-entropy against the orthographically-derived H/M/L label. Syllable boundary: the same per-token durations VITS already derives via monotonic alignment (attn.sum over the frame axis) are summed per syllable and compared (L1) against the verified syllable frame duration. Neither requires new annotation -- both are read off dataset/verified/training_batch_01_verified_alignments.jsonl via execution/condition_c/derive_tone_syllable_targets.py.

initialization.reason_optimizer_reset: avoid inherited optimizer moments dominating the 23-clip adaptation run; identical to Condition B

data.audio_normalization: original PCM scale only; no loudness normalization, trimming, denoising, or augmentation
data.text: authoritative NFC Yoruba; MMS vocabulary filtering and blank insertion only
data.tone_syllable_targets: derived at runtime from dataset/verified/training_batch_01_verified_alignments.jsonl via execution/condition_c/derive_tone_syllable_targets.py; train/development rows only, protected test rows excluded from generation

trainable_modules.generator: text encoder, flow, posterior encoder, and waveform decoder
trainable_modules.auxiliary_heads: one linear tone classifier (hidden_channels -> 3 classes: L/M/H) attached to the text encoder's per-token hidden state; no other new parameters

checkpoint_selection.selection_metric: mean development reconstruction objective: 45*mel_L1 + duration_nll + KL

randomness.scope: feasibility pilot; MMS already pronounces Yoruba relatively well so this comparison has a ceiling effect -- it tests whether the dataset, pipeline, and tone-aware method can refine an already-strong Yoruba model, not whether tone supervision is necessary for Yoruba TTS in general. Multi-seed replication required for confirmatory claims.

overfitting_safeguards: low 1e-5 learning rate from the full pretrained checkpoint, identical to Condition B
300-update hard cap, identical to Condition B
early stopping after four non-improving evaluations, but not before update 100
restore the best development checkpoint rather than the last checkpoint
no test-set access for selection, stopping, or auxiliary-target generation
auxiliary losses excluded from checkpoint-selection metric so they cannot be gamed by the selection rule itself
log train-development loss gap and flag a gap larger than 25 percent

compute.estimated_wall_time: approximately 30 to 120 minutes for the 300-update cap, same order as Condition B plus a small overhead for the extra encoder call and auxiliary losses; benchmark the first 10 updates and report the measured estimate

approval_gate: Do not download the archive, prepare a GPU runtime, update weights, or inspect protected test outputs until Mary Adelua approves this exact recipe.
